about: 26 hook formulas for Instagram Reels. Each is a move an opening makes, not a sentence to copy. 'source' says where it came from: 'research' formulas were derived from the spoken and on-screen hooks of top Reels (ranked by shares per view) collected with ig-research in November 2026; 'craft' formulas come from general short-video writing practice and have no measured result behind them here. Examples are made up. 'cues' are patterns hooks.py uses to suggest which formula a winner's hook resembles. Each cue needs the formula's defining feature (free AND a deadline, a number AND hidden things, can't AND a way now), so a hook that only shares a word matches nothing: abstaining beats a wrong name. The model confirms or corrects every match.

formulas.name: What it did for me
formulas.move: Open on one specific thing the tool did for you, in the past tense, with a number or a name in it.
formulas.template: My {tool} {did one specific thing} {for me / while I did something else}.
formulas.example: My AI read 300 job ads overnight and kept the 12 worth applying to.
formulas.use_when: You have a real result of your own and the tool is the surprise.

formulas.name: Someone else's moment
formulas.move: Tell a stranger's small, vivid problem and that the tool solved it, as a story you are passing on.
formulas.template: This {person} {had a specific problem}, so they {asked the tool}, and {what happened}.
formulas.example: This woman dropped her ring in a storm drain, sent one photo to an AI, and it told her which grate to lift.
formulas.on_screen: AI found her ring in a drain
formulas.use_when: The best example isn't yours, and the problem is one viewers have had.

formulas.name: Can't, until this
formulas.move: Name something viewers assume the tool cannot do, then say there is now a way.
formulas.template: {Tool} can't {thing people assume} until you {add / turn on this}.
formulas.example: Your AI can't see your calendar until you switch on one setting.
formulas.on_screen: Your AI can't see your calendar (yet)
formulas.use_when: The idea removes a limit people have run into themselves.

formulas.name: The overlooked tool
formulas.move: Say a tool is one few people know about, and give the one reason it matters in the same breath.
formulas.template: {Thing} is the most overlooked {category} right now, because it lets you {concrete benefit}.
formulas.example: This is the most overlooked browser setting right now, because it stops every site from autoplaying video.
formulas.use_when: The thing is real and little known, and its benefit fits in one clause.

formulas.name: Free, with a date
formulas.move: Lead with something of value given away, and the date it stops.
formulas.template: {Who} is giving {amount or thing} free, but only until {date}.
formulas.example: The city library is giving out free museum passes, but only until Friday.
formulas.use_when: There is a real offer with a real end date. Never invent one.

formulas.name: The swap
formulas.move: Set the new thing against the one viewers already use, as a replacement.
formulas.template: {New thing} just replaced {familiar thing} for me.
formulas.example: A free notes app just replaced the paid one I'd used for six years.
formulas.use_when: Most viewers use the familiar thing and would switch for a clear reason.

formulas.name: The question they ask
formulas.move: Open with the exact question a viewer would type into search, then answer it.
formulas.template: How do you {do the thing} {in the specific situation}?
formulas.example: How do you get your phone to stop waking you for group chats but not for your kids?
formulas.on_screen: Mute group chats, not your kids
formulas.use_when: It's a how-to people already search for; the answer is short.

formulas.name: Just out, my use
formulas.move: Name a launch, then skip the announcement and say the one thing you are already using it for.
formulas.template: {Thing} came out {when}, and I'm already using it to {specific job}.
formulas.example: The new camera app came out yesterday, and I'm already using it to scan receipts for my taxes.
formulas.use_when: It's news, and you have a use the launch videos didn't show.

formulas.name: Same test, two contenders
formulas.move: Give two options the same task and promise the result.
formulas.template: I gave {A} and {B} the same {task}. One {clear result}.
formulas.example: I gave two budgeting apps the same month of receipts. One missed $400.
formulas.use_when: You ran a fair comparison and the gap is big enough to show.

formulas.name: Hidden shortcuts, counted
formulas.move: Promise a small, exact number of things most people don't know exist.
formulas.template: {N} {shortcuts / settings / codes} for {thing} most people never find.
formulas.example: Three keyboard shortcuts for your phone camera most people never find.
formulas.use_when: Each item is quick to show and genuinely hidden.

formulas.name: Part N of a series
formulas.move: Label the Reel as one entry in a running list, so returning viewers know the format.
formulas.template: {Series title}, part {N}: {this entry}.
formulas.example: Things your phone can do that you never use, part 4: it measures a room.
formulas.use_when: You post a run of entries on one theme; works best once the series has followers.

formulas.name: Done in minutes
formulas.move: Promise the result and the exact time it takes to set up.
formulas.template: You can {get result} in {N minutes / seconds}.
formulas.example: You can give your front door camera a voice in 10 minutes.
formulas.use_when: Setup really is that quick, and the result is the draw.

formulas.name: While you were away
formulas.move: Show the work happening while you slept, left, or closed the laptop.
formulas.template: {Thing} kept {working / watching} while I {slept / left / closed the laptop}.
formulas.example: My laptop was shut all night and it still finished the edit.
formulas.use_when: The surprise is that nobody had to be there.

formulas.name: One ask, whole result
formulas.move: Show a finished result and say how little it took to ask for it.
formulas.template: I made {finished thing} with one {message / prompt}.
formulas.example: I made this whole birthday invite with one message.
formulas.use_when: The finished thing is on screen in the first second.

formulas.name: The cheaper way
formulas.move: Promise the same result for less money or less of something people pay for.
formulas.template: How to {get the same thing} for {N% less / free}.
formulas.example: How to get the same phone plan for half the price, without switching carriers.
formulas.use_when: You can show the saving with your own numbers.

formulas.name: What it cost me
formulas.move: Open on a loss you took, in money or time, then show what you do now.
formulas.template: {Doing it the old way} cost me {amount}.
formulas.example: Forgetting one renewal date cost me $240 last year.
formulas.use_when: There's a real, sizeable cost you paid yourself.

formulas.name: My mistake
formulas.move: Admit something you did wrong for a while, specifically, so viewers check whether they do it too.
formulas.template: For {time} I {did the wrong thing}.
formulas.example: For two years I charged my phone overnight on the wrong setting.
formulas.on_screen: I did this wrong for 2 years
formulas.use_when: The mistake is common and the fix is quick.

formulas.name: From this to that
formulas.move: Give the before and after as two numbers.
formulas.template: {Task} went from {before} to {after}.
formulas.example: My weekly grocery list went from 40 minutes to 5.
formulas.use_when: You measured both sides and the gap is large.

formulas.name: Stop doing this
formulas.move: Tell viewers to stop a specific habit, and name the habit exactly.
formulas.template: Stop {specific habit}.
formulas.example: Stop typing your address into every checkout page.
formulas.use_when: The habit is widespread and you have the better way ready.

formulas.name: If you're this person
formulas.move: Call out exactly who the Reel is for in the first words.
formulas.template: If you {specific situation}, {what to do / what you're missing}.
formulas.example: If you run a bakery and still take orders by phone, watch this.
formulas.use_when: The audience is narrow and they'd recognise themselves at once.
cues: ^if you('re| are| run| have| use| still)\b

formulas.name: The line someone said
formulas.move: Open on a quote, from a client, a friend or a comment, that sets up the story.
formulas.template: "{The exact line}," {who} said.
formulas.example: "Can it just tell me when the parcel arrives?" my neighbour asked.
formulas.use_when: Someone really said it, and it's the question your Reel answers.

formulas.name: In the middle of it
formulas.move: Start inside the moment as it happened, with no set-up, so the viewer wants to know how it ends.
formulas.template: {The moment, present or just past tense}, so I {what you did}.
formulas.example: The train stopped in a tunnel, so I asked my phone to tell me the second it moved.
formulas.use_when: You have a real scene with a clear problem in it.

formulas.name: Everyone says, I tried
formulas.move: State a common belief, then say you tested it and it went differently.
formulas.template: Everyone says {belief}. I tried it for {time}.
formulas.example: Everyone says meal prep saves money. I tracked it for a month.
formulas.on_screen: I tracked it for a month
formulas.use_when: You have your own test that complicates the belief.

formulas.name: The number first
formulas.move: Lead with one surprising, checkable number, then say what it means for the viewer.
formulas.template: {Number} {what it counts}. {Why it matters to you}.
formulas.example: Nine out of ten phone chargers in my house were the slow kind.
formulas.use_when: The number is real, sourced or yours, and surprising.

formulas.name: Result on screen first
formulas.move: Show the finished result in the first second and say only what it is; explain after.
formulas.template: This is {result}, and {how little it took}.
formulas.example: This is my whole week planned, and I didn't touch the calendar.
formulas.use_when: The result is visual and makes sense without explanation.

formulas.name: I tried it for N days
formulas.move: Promise what happened after you used something for a set time.
formulas.template: I used {thing} for {N days} instead of {usual}.
formulas.example: I used only voice notes for a week instead of typing.
formulas.on_screen: A week of voice notes only
formulas.use_when: You did the test and the outcome is interesting either way.
